parts.title: My weekend job in a café
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I started working at the Blue Teapot café six months ago. It is a small place run by a woman called Mrs Alvarez, and I work there every Saturday and Sunday from nine until three.

At first, everything went wrong. On my first morning, I dropped a tray of cups, and I gave a customer the wrong cake. I wanted to hide in the kitchen, but Mrs Alvarez only laughed and said that everyone breaks cups in their first week. After that, I felt much more relaxed.

The best part of the job is the regular customers. There is an old man who always orders the same tea and tells me a joke, and two students who come to study and stay for hours. I have learned all their names. The worst part is the noise from the coffee machine, which gives me a headache on busy mornings.

With my first month's pay, I bought a good pair of headphones, and I am saving the rest for a trip to Italy next summer. Mrs Alvarez has promised that if I work hard, she will teach me to make her famous lemon cake.

questions.explanation: She only laughed and said that everyone breaks cups in the first week.

questions.explanation: He says the best part is the regular customers.

questions.explanation: The coffee machine is noisy and gives him a headache.

parts.title: My sixteenth birthday dinner
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
For my sixteenth birthday, my parents took me to a restaurant in the old part of town. [1] I had walked past it many times, but I had never been inside.

We arrived at seven, and a waiter showed us to a table by the window. [2] My mother said it was the most beautiful table in the room. The menu was long, and I found it hard to choose.

In the end, I ordered a mushroom pasta, which was delicious. My father, who loves fish, asked the waiter for advice. [3] He recommended the grilled sea bass, and my father was very pleased with it.

After the main course, the lights suddenly went out. [4] Everyone in the restaurant sang "Happy Birthday" while a waiter carried a cake with candles to our table. I was so surprised that I could not speak.

It was the best birthday of my life. [5] I have promised myself that I will bring my own children to the same restaurant one day.
sentences: My brother could not come because of his exams.
The food was perfect, and everybody looked so happy.
At first, I thought there was a power cut.
The prices on the menu were higher than I had expected.
From there, we could see the river and the lights of the bridge.
The waiter was friendly and knew the menu very well.
It was a small place with red walls and old photographs.
We booked the table three weeks before.

gaps.explanation: The description of the small place leads to "I had walked past it many times".
"From there" refers to the table by the window, and the view explains why it was beautiful.
The waiter's knowledge explains why the father asked him for advice and why he "recommended" a dish.
"At first, I thought" explains the lights going out, before the birthday surprise.
The sentence sums up why it was the best birthday, before the promise.

parts.title: A cooking class
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: perpetua
turns.text: Good evening, and welcome to Tasty Hands Cooking School. We are a small school with only twelve students in each class, so everybody can ask questions. I'm Perpetua, and tonight we're going to make a three-course meal. Before we start, I want to say a few words about safety. The kitchen floor can be wet, so please walk slowly, and tie back long hair. The class starts at half past six and finishes at nine. There is a short break at eight, when you can have a cup of tea or a glass of water. First, we'll make tomato soup. The tomatoes are from a farm near the school, and they are very sweet. You'll need an apron, and you can borrow one from me. They are hanging on the hooks behind the door, and you should choose the right size. The knives are provided, but please be careful. Cut away from your body, and never leave a knife on the edge of the table. For the main course, we'll cook chicken with rice, and for dessert, we'll bake an apple cake. Everyone will get a small piece to take home in a box, so please bring a bag. The recipe sheets are on the table, and you can write notes on them. At nine o'clock, we'll all eat together at the long table. You can bring a guest to the meal, but please tell the office a day before. Each class costs thirty pounds, and the ingredients are included in the price. If you enjoy the class, there are six more evenings this month, and you can book them at the desk. Now, let's wash our hands and begin.

gaps.prompt: The class starts at half past ___
gaps.explanation: The class starts at half past six.
First, they will make tomato soup.
She says students can borrow an apron from her.

gaps.prompt: For dessert, they will bake an ___ cake
gaps.explanation: For dessert, they will bake an apple cake.

gaps.prompt: They will eat together at ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: They will all eat together at nine o'clock.

parts.title: A restaurant chef
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: My guest tonight is Marnie Flynn, the head chef at a busy city restaurant. Marnie, who taught you to cook?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: My grandmother. I stood on a chair beside her when I was ten years old, and she let me stir the sauce. I think I fell in love with cooking that day.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: What was your first job in a kitchen?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: I washed plates in a hotel when I was sixteen. It was hard work, and my hands were red all the time, but I watched the chefs and learned something new every day.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Did you study cooking?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Yes, I spent two years in a small town in Italy, working in a family kitchen. I learned that the best dishes are often the simplest.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Was it easy to go back home after Italy?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Not at all. I missed the small town, the market and the family I worked for. But I was happy to see my own city again, and I opened a little café with a friend.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: What is the hardest part of your job?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Standing for twelve hours without stopping. People imagine that it is glamorous, but my feet hurt by the end of every night.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: What do you eat after work?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Usually a bowl of cereal at midnight! Chefs eat very badly at home, because we cook for other people all day. On my day off, I cook a big meal for my friends.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: How many meals do you cook on a busy night?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: On Saturdays, we serve about two hundred, and everything has to arrive hot at the same time. It is like a team sport.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: What happens when something goes wrong?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: We stay calm. Last month a customer found a hair in the soup, and I went to the table myself to say sorry. Good restaurants always listen to their customers.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Any advice for people who want to cook?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Taste everything while you cook. Recipes are useful, but your own mouth tells you what is missing.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Do you like to try food from other countries?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Very much. When I travel, I go to markets before I visit the museums. I once ate a fruit in Thailand that smelled terrible but tasted wonderful.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: What are you planning for the future?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: I'm writing a recipe book with my grandmother's best dishes. She is ninety, and she checks every page.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Is there a dish you will never cook again?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Snails! I cooked them once for a special dinner, and the smell stayed in the kitchen for a week.

turns.speaker: hugh
turns.text: Would you like to open your own restaurant?

turns.speaker: marnie
turns.text: Maybe one day, a small one with only ten tables, where I know every guest by name.
